## NVENCForge 2.2.3: keep means keep

This release is about what happens to your files after a conversion. Quality and speed are exactly as in 2.2.2.

- **`-keep` no longer renames the original.** Two cases used to give a kept source a new name: an MKV that already had the target codec, and an MKV whose encode was discarded for saving too little. Both now get a lossless copy in `output`, and the original stays where and as it was.
- **`-mp4`: the MP4 is checked before the MKV goes.** The intermediate MKV is only deleted once the MP4 has passed the same result check as every other output. If it does not, the MKV is kept.
- **`-mp4`: an original inside a folder called `output` is safe.** Only a file in the `output` folder of its own source counts as a result. The folder name alone used to decide, so such an original could be repackaged and deleted.
- **`-mp4` with `-keep`: no second encode.** Running the same files again recognises the finished MP4 and skips it, instead of encoding everything once more and writing a numbered twin.
- **`-mp4`: a discarded encode still gives you an MP4.** An MKV source whose encode was not worth keeping is now repackaged into the MP4 you asked for, instead of only being renamed.
- **Help text:** the outdated paragraph saying `-mp4` skips AV1 files is gone. They are repackaged, as the rest of the help already said.

Good to know: where `-keep` used to rename, there is now a copy in `output` next to the untouched original. That takes space, and it is what `-keep` promises.

Update: replace `NVENCForge.exe` with the new one. Your settings stay. With NVENCForgeGUI: use the converter's update button.
